newsitem.title: UK: Four green rates to be devalued on Sunday - HGCA.
newsitem.headline: Four green rates to be devalued on Sunday - HGCA.

text.p: The green rates of the mark, Belgian franc, guilder and the Austrian schilling will be devalued in the European Union's (EU) agrimonetary system on Sunday, the UK Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said on Friday.

It calculated the new green rates as 1.93473 per Ecu for the mark from previous 1.92441, 39.8740 for the Belgian franc from 39.6918, 2.17067 for the guilder from 2.15852 and 13.6155 for the schilling from 13.5396.
The devaluations were triggered by the strength of the Irish pound in the agrimonetary grid during a 10-day reference period which effectively ended on Friday.
The green rate of the Irish pound will enter its second of possibly five 10-day confirmation periods on Sunday for a revaluation currently forecast on January 11.
Also on Sunday, green sterling will enter its first of possibly five confirmation periods. It faces an agrimonetary revaluation on January 21 if sterling remains strong in exchange markets.
Green rates are used for calculating EU farm subsidies and support prices in national currencies.
